facts.statement: This dinosaur lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now China.
facts.quote: that lived during the Late Cretaceous in the area of present China.

facts.statement: The species Zuoyunlong huangi was named and described in 2017 by a team led by Wang Runfu.
facts.quote: In 2017 the type species Zuoyunlong huangi was named and described by Wang Runfu, You Hailu, Wang Suozhu, Shichao Xu, Yi Jian, Xie Lijuan, Lei Jia, and Xing Hai.

facts.statement: The preserved length of the ilium is 62 cm.
facts.quote: The ilium has a preserved length of 62 cm.

facts.statement: The 62 cm length of the preserved ilium suggests a total body length of nearly 8 meters.
facts.quote: El ilion tiene una longitud preservada de 62 centímetros, lo que indica una longitud corporal de cerca de 8 metros.

facts.statement: The ilium shaft ends in a large 'boot' shape pointing obliquely downwards and forwards in side view.
facts.quote: El eje del ilion termina en vista lateral en una "bota" grande la cual apunta hacia abajo y hacia adelante de manera oblicua.

facts.statement: Zuoyunlong lived during the Cenomanian stage, between 101 and 95 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados el período Cretácico, entre 101 a 95 millones des años, durante el Cenomaniense

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis places Zuoyunlong in a basal position within Hadrosauroidea as the sister taxon of Probactrosaurus.
facts.quote: A cladistic analysis found that Zuoyunlong had a basal position in the Hadrosauroidea, as sister taxon of Probactrosaurus.

facts.statement: The time range for Zuoyunlong is estimated from 100.5 to 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Santonian (100.5 to 83.6 million years ago)
